rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghabun adds expiation of sins for unbelievers invited to faith, whose sins continue; Talaq addresses believers urged to obey God, so the addition fits Taghabun better.
rows.anchor: فكن ذكر تكفير السيئات مع الكافرين الذين هم في معصية مستديمة وسيئاتهم غير منقطعة أولى من ذكرها مع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman adds deafness in the ears because it has not already described the person hearing the verses; al-Jathiyah explicitly says he hears them, making deafness incongruous, while Luqman has added wrongdoing in its context.
rows.anchor: فوصْفُه بسماعٍ آياتِ لله لم يكن ليطابقه ذِكْرُ الوقر في الأذن لأنه قد ذكر سماعه الآيات. والوقر مانع من السماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma'idah adds “beware” and “know” after its emphatic prohibition of intoxicants and related evils; al-Taghabun has no comparable preceding prohibition, so the extra warning is unnecessary there.
rows.anchor: فناسب ذلك ذكر هذه الزيادة لتأكيد التحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fath adds “for you” because it addresses specific lagging Bedouins; al-Ma'idah addresses people generally, including everyone on earth, so the phrase is omitted.
rows.anchor: فلما كان الخطاب مختصاً بهؤلاء زاد (لكم) لأن الخطاب موجه إليهم

rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: Durrat al-Tanzil says the Fath address concerned Bedouins who lagged without excuse, blamed family obligations, then sought the Prophet's forgiveness to conceal hypocrisy and win his favor.
rows.anchor: جاء في (درة التنزيل) عن سبب ذلك (لكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-'Ankabut adds “nor in heaven” amid its account of peoples who denied messengers and were punished, extending the challenge even to those reaching heaven; al-Shura concerns worldly misfortunes.
rows.anchor: كان الكلام في العنكبوت في سياق تكذيب الأنبياء ومحاربة الرسل ومعاقبة الله لهؤلاء الأقوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma'idah details the full ablution and tayammum rulings, so it adds “from it” for clarification; al-Nisa' gives only some rulings and aptly leaves the phrase out.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه حيث كان السياق مجملاً أجمل في الذكر، وحيث كان مفصّلاً مبيناً زاد وبيّن

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani likewise says al-Nisa' mentions only some ablution and tayammum rulings, making omission apt, while al-Ma'idah gives all the rulings and therefore states the phrase.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني: أنه اد في آية المائدة (منه)

words: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ فِي الأرض وَلاَ في أَنفُسِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author offers al-Hadid's added detail about where calamity occurs and its prior record as a parallel case where fuller wording suits a more detailed statement than al-Taghabun.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذه الزيادة للتفصيل ما جاء في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah puts hearts first because the passage describes diseased hearts; al-Jathiyah puts hearing first because its context describes people hearing God's verses and refusing them.
rows.anchor: فقدم القلوب لذلك. وفي الجاثية ذكر الأسماع المعطلة فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the preposition “upon” for hearts and hearing in al-Baqarah intensifies the description of the seal; al-Jathiyah uses one preposition for both.
rows.anchor: ثم كرر حرف الجر (على) مع القلوب والأسماع في آية البقرة مما يفيد توكيد الختم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah's nominal clause depicts a lasting veil and no prospect of sight; al-Jathiyah's past-tense verb “placed” indicates a later occurrence, and “upon knowledge” implies he once saw.
rows.anchor: والجملة الاسمية كما هو معلوم تفيد الدوام والثبات، ومعنى ذلك أن هؤلاء لم يسبق لهم أن أبصروا

words: سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah portrays more deeply entrenched disbelief than al-Jathiyah: warning or not makes no difference to its people, and its ending adds a great punishment.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن صفات الكفر في البقرة أشد تمكناً فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is the locus of guidance and misguidance; once sealed, hearing and sight cannot help. Qur'an 22:46 likewise says blindness is in hearts, supporting the order in al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: فإن القلب هو محل الهدى والضلال، وإذا ختم عليه فلا ينفع سمع ولا بصر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares the heart to a morsel: when it is sound the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt the whole body is corrupt.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا وإنَّ في الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml fronts “this” because its preceding claim makes the speakers and their fathers dust, a greater decay and stronger occasion for amazement than the dust-and-bones wording in al-Mu'minun.
rows.anchor: فالجهة المنظور فيها هناك كونهم أنفسهم وآباؤهم تراباً. والجهة المنظرو فيها هنا كونهم تراباً وعظاماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-An'am puts the declaration of God's oneness before “creator of everything” because the surrounding passage rejects partners, spouses, and offspring and calls for pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أن لكلام على التوحيد ونفي الشرك والشركاء والصاحبة والولد ولذا قدم كلمة التوحيد

words: خالق كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لاَّ إلاه إِلاَّ هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ghafir, the discussion turns from prayer and God's favors, including night and day, to creation; thus “creator of everything” comes before “no deity but He.”
rows.anchor: فالكلام كما ترى على الخَلْق وعلى نعم الله وفضله على الناس لا على التوحيد فقدم الخلق لذلك

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani explains that al-An'am rejects partners and offspring, so it leads with “no deity but He,” whereas Ghafir follows a discussion of creation and leads with God's creative act.
rows.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني: "قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfal foregrounds wealth because ransom and booty had drawn attention and sacrifice was needed; al-Tawbah foregrounds God's path because its context stresses jihad.
rows.anchor: فقدم المال ههنا، لأن المال كان مطلوباً لهم حتى عاتبهم الله في ذلك فطلب أن يبدؤوا بالتضيحة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes the reversed order in Fatir; in Nahl, “cleaving” follows a preceding sequence about transport, where ships are introduced as another means of travel.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه تقدم الكلام في النحل على وسائط النقل، فذكر الأنعام وأنها تحمل الأثقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran adds that God will not look at the offenders because they not only conceal truth but corrupt it and swear falsely for a small price, a graver offense than concealment alone.
rows.anchor: فلما زادوا في الذنب زاد الله لهم في العقوبة فقال: (ولا ينظر إليهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added punishment also fits Al Imran's preceding concern with keeping God's covenant (3:76), whereas al-Baqarah's preceding passage concerns forbidden foods (2:173).
rows.anchor: فلما كان المقام في آل عمران هو الكلام على عهد الله ناسب تشديد العقوبة على مضيعيه أكثر مما في البقرة
